mainTopic: Can animals that came from a non-Jew be brought as קרבנות? The גמרא answers challenges from פסוקים, ending with the song of the cows that carried the ארון.
overview: The background worry in this sugya is that a non-Jew may have used his animal for רביעה (bestiality), which would make it unfit for the מזבח. The גמרא tests this worry against cases where animals linked to non-Jews seem to have been offered. יתרו bought his animals from a Jew. The 'best' animals of עמלק were meant to be sold, and the money used to buy other animals. ארונה was a גר תושב, so he was not suspected. The cows of the פלשתים that pulled the ארון were offered under a הוראת שעה, a one-time ruling. The supporting argument that a female עולה is otherwise impossible is pushed aside, since a female עולה is allowed on a במת יחיד. רבי יוחנן then offers a new approach: a non-Jew would not abuse an animal under three years old, because it would become barren. That answer fails for the cows, which already had calves, so the גמרא returns to the הוראת שעה answer. The amud ends with אגדה about the song the cows sang to the ארון, and two Persian words traced back to פסוקים.

steps.title: What about the view that יתרו came after מתן תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The earlier answer, that יתרו brought his offerings before מתן תורה, does not work for the opinion that he came afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the view that יתרו came after the Torah was given, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing the question about יתרו's offerings. It points out that the earlier answer only works for one opinion about when יתרו arrived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer said that before מתן תורה there was no concern about animals from non-Jews. But one opinion holds that יתרו came after מתן תורה. By then the concern applied, so how could Jews accept and offer his animals?

keyTerms.meaning: The giving of the Torah at הר סיני
What is there to say? This signals a problem that still needs an answer

steps.confusionAlert: This step starts in the middle of a thought. The words 'according to the one who says' come just before it. The גמרא is not stating as fact that יתרו came after מתן תורה. It is only asking about the opinion that says so.

phrases.english: [According to the one who says] Yitro came after the giving of the Torah,
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets fill in what the גמרא assumes from just before this line. There is a debate about when יתרו arrived.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the earlier answer about יתרו does not cover every opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that animals from non-Jews may not be offered, given that יתרו's offerings were accepted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If יתרו came after מתן תורה, the concern about animals from non-Jews already applied, so his offerings should have been unfit.

steps.title: Yitro bought his animals from a Jew
steps.stepSummary: יתרו's animals were bought from a Jew, so the concern about non-Jewish animals never applied to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, יתרו bought the animals from a Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about יתרו. His animals were bought from a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is only about an animal that was in a non-Jew's hands. If יתרו bought his animals from a Jew, the animals were never under that suspicion. So the rule stands even if יתרו came after מתן תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. This brings in a new answer

phrases.english: Rather, Yitro bought [the animals] from a Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: the animals came from a Jew
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יתרו was a non-Jew offering his own animals
steps.terutzMaskana: He bought the animals from a Jew, so they were never under suspicion
steps.whatToRemember: The concern is about animals that were owned by a non-Jew. An animal bought from a Jew is not suspected.

steps.title: Challenge from שאול and the animals of עמלק
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק says the people spared the best of עמלק's animals in order to sacrifice them to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: שאול said, 'They brought them from עמלק, because the people spared the best of the sheep and cattle to sacrifice to ה׳ your God.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge from a פסוק. It looks like the people planned to offer animals that had belonged to non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals of עמלק were owned by non-Jews. Yet the פסוק says they were saved in order to be sacrificed. This suggests such animals are fine for the מזבח.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And Saul said: They have brought them from the Amalekites,
phrases.notes: שמואל א 15:15

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר חָמַל הָעָם עַל מֵיטַב הַצֹּאן וְהַבָּקָר
phrases.english: for the people spared the best of the flock and of the herd,
(the second-born, and the fatlings, and all the flock)
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. They come from an earlier פסוק and are not part of this one.

phrases.english: to sacrifice to the Lord your God"!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וַיֹּאמֶר שָׁאוּל מֵעֲמָלֵקִי הֱבִיאוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with יתרו, the גמרא brings a second challenge from a פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule against offering animals that came from non-Jews
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The people planned to offer animals taken from עמלק, a non-Jewish nation. That suggests such animals are acceptable.

steps.title: 'The best' means the money value of the best
steps.stepSummary: The people planned to sell the best animals and use the money to buy other animals for קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'the best' mean? The value of the best animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading the פסוק. The people meant to offer what the best animals were worth, not the animals themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animals would be sold and the money used to buy other animals, then no animal from עמלק would ever reach the מזבח. So the פסוק does not show that non-Jewish animals may be offered.

phrases.english: What is "the best"?
The value of the best.
phrases.notes: He means they would sell the animals and buy other ones for קרבנות with the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the פסוק about שאול.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The best animals themselves would be offered
steps.terutzMaskana: Only their money value would be used, to buy other animals

steps.title: Why save the best animals in particular?
steps.stepSummary: If only the money matters, why did they choose the best animals?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is special about the best ones?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about its own answer. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the plan was only to sell, any animals would do. So why did they pick the best ones? The answer must explain this choice.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why this one in particular?

phrases.english: And what is different about the best?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the answer given in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the best animals were chosen if they would only be sold

steps.title: Good animals sell easily
steps.stepSummary: They chose the best animals so that buyers would rush to buy them.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that buyers would jump at them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the choice: the best animals are the easiest to sell.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Buyers want high-quality animals, so these would sell quickly. This fits the reading that the money, not the animals, was meant for the קרבנות. The reading of the פסוק from step 4 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Will jump at, rush to grab

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק about שאול is no proof. The animals of עמלק were to be sold, and the money used to buy other animals for the מזבח.

phrases.english: So that buyers would jump at them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The best animals sell more easily, so they would bring in money quickly.

steps.title: Challenge from ארונה's offer to דוד
steps.stepSummary: ארונה, a non-Jew, offered his cattle to דוד for an עולה, and it seems the offer was acceptable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: ארונה said to דוד, 'Let my lord the king take and offer what he thinks is good. See, here are the cattle for the עולה, and the threshing boards and the cattle's equipment for wood.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third challenge from a פסוק. A non-Jew offered his own cattle as a קרבן to דוד המלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ארונה was a non-Jew, and his cattle came straight from him. The offer seems to have been a proper one. This suggests animals from non-Jews may be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: The non-Jewish owner of the threshing floor that דוד bought
A burnt offering, burned fully on the מזבח

phrases.english: Come and hear:
"And Araunah said to David:
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 24:22

phrases.english: Let my lord the king take and offer up
what seems good to him; behold the cattle for the burnt offering,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets. The word in square brackets, רְאֵה ('behold'), is the correct wording of the פסוק.

phrases.english: and the threshing boards and the equipment of the cattle for wood"!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: וַיֹּאמֶר אֲרַוְנָה אֶל דָּוִד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After answering the challenge from שאול, the גמרא brings a third challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule against offering animals that came from non-Jews
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A non-Jew offered his own cattle as an עולה for דוד, and the offer seems acceptable.

steps.title: ארונה was a גר תושב
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that ארונה was a גר תושב, so his animals were not suspected.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: ארונה was a גר תושב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the challenge from ארונה. ארונה was a גר תושב, a non-Jew who had accepted the seven מצוות בני נח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seven מצוות בני נח forbid רביעה (bestiality). A non-Jew who keeps them is trusted not to have done it with his animals. So ארונה's cattle were fine, and the general concern about other non-Jews' animals still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who accepted the seven מצוות בני נח
The seven commandments for all non-Jews

steps.whatToRemember: The concern is about a non-Jew who is suspected of רביעה. A גר תושב keeps the seven מצוות בני נח, so he is not suspected, and his animals may be offered.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the concern is not about non-Jews as such. It is about whether the owner is suspected of mistreating the animal in a forbidden way.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
Araunah was a ger toshav.
phrases.notes: A גר תושב keeps the seven מצוות בני נח, which forbid bestiality. So his animals are not suspected.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אֲרַוְנָה גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from ארונה in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case: this owner was not an ordinary non-Jew
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ארונה was an ordinary non-Jew, suspected like any other
steps.terutzMaskana: ארונה was a גר תושב who keeps the מצוות בני נח, so his animals were not suspected

steps.title: What does the word מורגים mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא steps aside to ask the meaning of the word מורגים from the ארונה story.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are מורגים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the main discussion to ask what a word from the ארונה פסוק means. This is a side question about a word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ארונה story, he offered דוד the cattle and also the מורגים to use as firewood. The גמרא wants to know exactly what these objects were.

phrases.english: What are 'morigim'?
phrases.notes: This word comes from the ארונה פסוק we just saw (שמואל ב 24:22), where he offers his מורגים as firewood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Side question about a word in the ארונה פסוק brought in step 7
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word מורגים

steps.title: עולא: It is a טורביל bed
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that מורגים are a 'טורביל bed'.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: It is a טורביל bed.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers that a מורג is something called a 'טורביל bed'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer gives a name for the object but is still unclear, so the גמרא will ask for more explanation right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'טורביל bed', a kind of threshing board

phrases.english: Ulla said:
A turbil bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9

steps.title: What is a טורביל bed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a טורביל bed is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a טורביל bed?
steps.whatsHappening: The answer of עולא used an unfamiliar term, so the גמרא asks what it means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a follow-up question. The גמרא wants to turn the strange name into a clear description.

phrases.english: What is a turbil bed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of the term עולא used
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What object a טורביל bed is

steps.title: A toothed board used for threshing
steps.stepSummary: A טורביל bed is a toothed wooden board used to thresh grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a toothed board used by threshers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that it is a wooden board with jagged teeth that is dragged over grain to thresh it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we finally know what ארונה offered as firewood: wooden threshing boards. They were made of wood, so they could be burned.

phrases.english: A toothed board of the threshers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A serrated wooden board used for threshing

steps.title: רב יוסף brings a פסוק that shows a מורג threshes
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף brings a פסוק in ישעיהו showing that a מורג is a toothed threshing board.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is the פסוק that shows this? 'Behold, I have made you a new sharp threshing board with many teeth; you will thresh mountains and crush them, and make hills like chaff.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף backs up the explanation with a פסוק that uses the word מורג for a threshing tool with teeth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses מורג together with 'having teeth' and 'threshing'. That matches the toothed threshing board that was just described, so the word study is complete.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק (that teaches this)?

steps.whatToRemember: מורגים are wooden threshing boards with teeth. That is why ארונה could offer them as firewood.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What is the verse?
"Behold, I have made you a new sharp threshing board
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 41:15

phrases.english: having teeth;
you shall thresh mountains and crush them,
and make hills like chaff."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק that supports the definition in step 12
steps.raayaObject: That a מורג is a toothed threshing board

steps.title: The פלשתים's cows were offered as an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that animals of non-Jews are suspect, from the cows of the פלשתים that were offered as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged this: 'And they offered the cows as an עולה to ה׳'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the main topic and challenges it. When the ארון came back from the פלשתים, the cows that pulled it were offered as an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Those cows belonged to non-Jews, and yet the Jews offered them without worry. That seems to go against the opinion that animals of non-Jews are suspect and may not be used.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt-offering, burned completely on the מזבח

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
"And they offered the cows as a burnt-offering to the Lord"!
phrases.notes: שמואל א 6:14. These are the cows the פלשתים sent pulling the ארון back home.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side trip about the word, the גמרא brings a new challenge to the main topic
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion (רבי אליעזר) that animals of non-Jews are suspect and may not be used for holy purposes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Jews offered the פלשתים's cows as an עולה, so animals of non-Jews must be acceptable

steps.title: It was a one-time ruling
steps.stepSummary: The cows were offered under a special one-time ruling (הוראת שעה), so there is no proof from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a one-time ruling for that moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that offering those cows was a special emergency ruling for that moment only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הוראת שעה does not teach us the normal halacha. So the cows tell us nothing about whether animals of non-Jews are usually allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A one-time special ruling for unusual circumstances

steps.confusionAlert: A הוראת שעה is not the regular rule. You cannot learn the normal halacha from it.

phrases.english: It was a provisional ruling for the hour.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a one-time exception (הוראת שעה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cows prove that animals of non-Jews are normally allowed
steps.terutzMaskana: The cows were a special exception and teach nothing about the normal rule

steps.title: Support: a female עולה does not normally exist
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports the הוראת שעה answer: the cows were female, and a female עולה is normally not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. Because if you do not say so, is there such a thing as a female עולה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds support for its answer. The cows were female, and an עולה must normally be male.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Offering a female as an עולה breaks the normal rules anyway. So the whole event must have been a special one-time ruling, and this strengthens the answer in step 15.

phrases.english: So too it stands to reason,
for if you do not say so,
is there such a thing as a female burnt-offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives logical support to the answer of step 15
steps.raayaObject: That the cows were offered under a הוראת שעה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The normal rule that an עולה must be male, yet these cows were female

steps.title: Maybe it was on a private altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the support: perhaps the cows were offered on a במת יחיד, where a female עולה is allowed, following רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difficulty? Perhaps it was on a private altar, following רב אדא בר אהבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the support from step 16. Maybe the female cows were not a problem at all, because they were offered on a private altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a female עולה is allowed on a במת יחיד, then the female cows do not show that anything unusual happened. The support for הוראת שעה falls away, but the answer of step 15 itself still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A private altar, used by an individual when such altars were allowed

phrases.english: And what is the difficulty?
Perhaps it was on a private altar,
and in line with Rav Adda bar Ahava,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the support given in step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the supporting argument of step 16, not the answer of הוראת שעה itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A female עולה is allowed on a private altar, so the female cows prove nothing unusual

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה's source: שמואל's milk lamb
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה learns from שמואל's offering of a milk lamb that a female עולה is allowed on a במת יחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב אדא בר אהבה said: Where do we learn that a female עולה is allowed on a private altar? As it says: 'And שמואל took one milk lamb and offered it as an עולה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רב אדא בר אהבה's source. שמואל offered a 'milk lamb', a female, as an עולה on a private altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proves that a female עולה is allowed on a במת יחיד. That backs up the rejection in step 17, so the female cows do not prove that the event was a הוראת שעה.

keyTerms.meaning: A milk lamb, understood here as female

steps.whatToRemember: The cows of the פלשתים are explained as a הוראת שעה. The female-עולה argument does not prove this, since a female עולה is allowed on a במת יחיד.

phrases.english: for Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
From where do we know that a female burnt-offering
is valid on a private altar?
As it is stated:
"And Samuel took one milk lamb
phrases.notes: שמואל א 7:9. A 'milk lamb' is taken to mean a female.

phrases.english: and offered it as a burnt-offering."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: מִנַּיִן לְעוֹלָה נְקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the rule used in the rejection of step 17
steps.raayaObject: That a female עולה is valid on a private altar

steps.title: The verse calls שמואל's lamb a male
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects to רב אדא בר אהבה's proof. The word ויעלהו in the פסוק is masculine, which suggests שמואל's lamb was a male.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ויעלהו, 'he offered HIM.' That sounds like the lamb was a male!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the proof from step 18. If the lamb was a male, it tells us nothing about offering a female עולה on a במת יחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה needed שמואל's lamb to be female. The masculine ending '-הו' ('him') suggests it was male. If so, his proof falls apart.

phrases.english: 'And he offered him' implies a male!
phrases.notes: שמואל א 7:9, the פסוק about שמואל's milk lamb from the previous step.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof brought in step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא בר אהבה's proof from שמואל's lamb
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The masculine grammar of the פסוק suggests the lamb was male, so it cannot prove anything about a female עולה.

steps.title: The word is written in the feminine
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the written letters spell ויעלה, which can be read as feminine ('her').
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: the word is written ויעלה, 'he offered HER.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends the proof. The way the word is written, not the way it is read aloud, shows the lamb was female.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is read as ויעלהו but spelled without the ו at the end, so it can be read as ויעלה, 'her.' The גמרא learns from the spelling that the lamb was female. So רב אדא בר אהבה's proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written (how the word is spelled)

steps.confusionAlert: Some words in תנ״ך are read one way but spelled another. The גמרא here learns from the spelling, not the reading.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
It is written 'and he offered her.'
phrases.notes: He means the spelling. It is read as 'him,' but the letters can be read as 'her.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the פסוק based on its spelling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lamb was male, so there is no proof about a female עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The spelling shows the lamb was female, so a female עולה is allowed on a במת יחיד.
steps.whatToRemember: The cows of the פלשתים could have been offered on a במת יחיד, where a female עולה is allowed. So they do not prove a הוראת שעה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the line is at three years old
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives a new approach. A non-Jew would not abuse an animal under three years old, because it would become barren.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: there is a clear dividing line. If the animal is under three years old, it becomes barren. If it is three, it does not become barren.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new way to explain when animals bought from non-Jews may be used as קרבנות. רבי יוחנן draws a line based on the animal's age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under three, the abuse would make the animal barren, so a non-Jew would not risk ruining his own animal. Animals from non-Jews are therefore only suspect from age three and up. This lets רבי יוחנן allow younger animals as קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: A border; a clear dividing line
Becomes barren (can no longer have young)

steps.whyThisMatters: This age rule becomes רבי יוחנן's tool for answering every challenge that follows.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: גְּבוּל יֵשׁ לָהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: There is a dividing line for it:
phrases.notes: 'It' is an animal that a person abused. Its age decides whether a non-Jew would be suspected.

phrases.english: under three years old, she becomes barren;
three years old, she does not become barren.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר גְּבוּל יֵשׁ לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing with the challenges to the earlier view, the גמרא brings a separate approach by רבי יוחנן to when animals from non-Jews may be offered. The following steps test it against the earlier challenges.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal under three would become barren from abuse, so a non-Jew is not suspected with it. From age three, he is suspected.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן answers all the challenges the same way
steps.stepSummary: All the earlier challenges were raised against רבי יוחנן. He answered every one by saying the animals were under three.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised all those challenges against him, and he answered them: the animals were under three years old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sums up how רבי יוחנן deals with all the earlier proofs that non-Jews' animals were used as קרבנות. Each one involved animals younger than three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, each proof needed its own answer. Now one rule answers all of them: the animals were under three, so they were never suspect.

phrases.english: They challenged him with all these challenges,
phrases.notes: These are the earlier proofs that animals from non-Jews were brought as קרבנות.

phrases.aramaic: שַׁנִּי לְהוּ: פְּחוּתָה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: he answered them: under three years old.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ כֹּל הָנֵי תְּיוּבָתָא שַׁנִּי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of step 21 to all the earlier challenges
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case: the animals were under the age of suspicion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Animals from non-Jews were used as קרבנות, which seems to contradict the suspicion against them.
steps.terutzMaskana: Those animals were under three, so there was no suspicion.

steps.title: The cows of the פלשתים were under three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the cows of the פלשתים offered as an עולה. By רבי יוחנן's approach, they were under three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And they offered the cows as an עולה to ה׳.' This was with cows under three years old.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows one example of רבי יוחנן's answer, using the case from step 14. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא needed a הוראת שעה to explain these cows. רבי יוחנן says no special ruling is needed: the cows were under three, so the פלשתים were not suspected with them.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'And they offered the cows as a burnt-offering to the Lord'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 6:14

phrases.english: — this was with ones under three years old.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע וְאֶת הַפָּרוֹת הֶעֱלוּ עֹלָה לַה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a specific example of the general answer in step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case by the animals' age
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cows of the פלשתים were suspect, so offering them needed a special ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cows were under three, so they were never suspect.

steps.title: Those cows already had calves
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges רבי יוחנן. The פסוק says these cows had calves, so can we really say they were under three?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, son of רב נתן, objected: If so, then 'and they shut their calves in the house' would also be about cows under three?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן attacks רבי יוחנן's answer for the cows of the פלשתים. The same cows are described as mothers with calves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the cows were under three. But another פסוק says these were nursing cows whose calves were shut in at home. The question is whether cows that already gave birth could still be under three.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Natan, challenged this:
If so, then this would be
'and they shut up their calves at home'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 6:10. The same cows, which were nursing their calves.

phrases.english: — cows under three years old?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן אִם כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that the cows of the פלשתים were under three
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cows already had calves. That makes it hard to say they were young enough to be under three.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows a cow under three does not give birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the challenge from step 24. A ברייתא shows that a cow under three years old does not give birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can a cow under three years old give birth? But a ברייתא teaches: if a Jew buys a cow or donkey from a non-Jew when it is under three, its next baby is certainly a בכור for the כהן. If it was older than that, it is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof for the challenge in step 24. The cows had calves, and a cow under three cannot give birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a young animal's next baby is certainly a firstborn, so it could not have given birth before. An older animal might have given birth already while it belonged to the non-Jew, so its baby is a doubt. This means cows that had calves were over three, which breaks רבי יוחנן's answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly goes to the כהן (as a בכור)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not about non-Jews abusing animals. It is about the law of בכור. The גמרא only uses it to learn a fact: animals under three do not give birth.

phrases.english: And one less than three years old
does it give birth?
But isn't it taught:
A cow or a donkey under three years old, bought from a non-Jew —
phrases.notes: This is about the law of בכור, the firstborn animal that belongs to the כהן.

phrases.english: its next offspring certainly goes to the priest,
from this age on, it is a doubt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְחוּתָה מִבַּת שָׁלֹשׁ שָׁנִים מִי קָא יָלְדָה? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 24 by bringing a ברייתא as proof.
steps.raayaObject: The challenge that the cows of the פלשתים could not have been under three
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about the law of בכור for animals bought from a non-Jew

steps.title: Going back to the first answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's approach is dropped. The גמרא returns to the answer it gave at the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear as we answered at first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on the 'under three years' idea. It goes back to its earlier answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא proved the cows were old enough to give birth, so רבי יוחנן's answer cannot explain them. The גמרא falls back on its first explanation: the עולה offered from these cows was a one-time special ruling for that moment.

keyTerms.meaning: As we answered at the beginning

steps.whatToRemember: The cows of the פלשתים had calves, so they were over three. The 'under three' answer fails, and the עולה is explained by the first answer, a one-time special ruling.

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear
as we answered at first.
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier answer, before רבי יוחנן's idea: offering the cows was a one-time special ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the result of the proof in step 25.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's answer is rejected for the cows of the פלשתים. The original answer stands.

steps.title: What does וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק about the cows going to בית שמש and asks what the unusual word וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the cows went straight (וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה) on the road, on the way to בית שמש.' What does וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new discussion about the same cows. It asks about one strange word in the פסוק and sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה could simply mean 'they went straight.' But it sounds like שירה, a song. The גמרא wants to know what the word is hinting at.

keyTerms.meaning: And they went straight (also sounds like 'they sang')
The town where the cows brought the ארון
And so on (the rest of the פסוק)

phrases.english: "And the cows went straight on the road,
phrases.notes: שמואל א 6:12

phrases.english: on the way to Beit Shemesh, etc."
What is "vayyisharna"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new אגדה topic about the same cows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה

steps.title: The cows sang a song
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי מאיר, says וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה means the cows sang a שירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי מאיר: it means they said a song.
steps.whatsHappening: The first answer reads וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה as coming from the word שירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר hears the sound of 'song' in the word. So the cows did not only walk straight. They sang praise as they carried the ארון.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
That they said a song.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: וַיִּשַּׁרְנָה means they sang a שירה.

steps.title: They turned to face the ארון and sang
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted by רב זוטרא בר טוביה, says the cows straightened their faces toward the ארון and sang.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא בר טוביה said in the name of רב: they straightened their faces toward the ארון and said a song.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer combines both meanings of the word: going straight and singing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב reads the word as 'straight' (יָשָׁר), meaning the cows turned their faces straight toward the ארון. He also keeps the idea of song, so the word means both.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Zutra bar Toviyya said in the name of Rav:
That they straightened their faces toward the Ark
and said a song.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב זוּטְרָא בַּר טוֹבִיָּה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer that adds 'straightening' to the song reading of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cows faced the ארון and sang.

steps.title: Which song did they sing?
steps.stepSummary: Both answers agree the cows sang, so the גמרא asks which song it was.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what song did they say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. It sets up a list of opinions about which song the cows sang.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 28 and 29 both say the cows sang. The open question now is the words of the song.

phrases.english: And what song did they say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up on the answers of steps 28 and 29.

steps.title: They sang שירת הים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי מאיר, says they sang אז ישיר, the song משה and בני ישראל sang at the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי מאיר: 'Then משה and בני ישראל sang.'
steps.whatsHappening: The first opinion names the song: שירת הים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cows sang the same song בני ישראל sang after crossing the sea. It is the classic song of thanks after a great rescue.

keyTerms.meaning: Then he sang (the opening of the Song of the Sea)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Meir:
"Then Moses and the children of Israel sang"
phrases.notes: שמות 15:1

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר אָז יָשִׁיר מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first answer to step 30.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's own view: a song from ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, in his own name, says the song was 'ואמרתם ביום ההוא הודו לה׳.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן himself said: 'And on that day you will say: Give thanks to ה׳, call out His name.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different song in his own name, not the one he quoted from רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן passed on רבי מאיר's view, but his own opinion is different. He picks a song of thanks from ישעיהו.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן says two things here. First he passes on רבי מאיר's view (step 31), then he gives his own different view. These are not contradicting statements of one opinion.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan himself said:
"And you shall say on that day:
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 12:4

phrases.english: Give thanks to the Lord, call out His name, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 30, from רבי יוחנן himself.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The song was ואמרתם ביום ההוא הודו לה׳.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: an 'orphaned' psalm
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש says it was the psalm 'מזמור שירו לה׳ שיר חדש,' a psalm with no named author.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: an orphaned psalm, 'A psalm: Sing to ה׳ a new song, for He did wonders; His right hand and His holy arm saved for Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion picks a song from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This psalm is called 'orphaned' because it does not say who wrote it or what event it is about. Its theme is a new song for wonders and rescue, which fits the ארון returning.

keyTerms.meaning: An orphaned psalm (no named author or event)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
An orphaned psalm,
phrases.notes: He means a psalm that does not say who wrote it or what it is about.

phrases.english: "A psalm: Sing to the Lord a new song,
phrases.notes: תהלים 98:1

phrases.english: for He has done wonders;
His right hand and His holy arm brought Him salvation."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר מִזְמוֹרָא יַתְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The song was תהלים 98, מזמור שירו לה׳ שיר חדש.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: 'ה׳ מלך ירגזו עמים'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the song was the psalm 'ה׳ מלך ירגזו עמים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: 'ה׳ reigns; let the nations tremble.'
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth opinion names a different psalm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This psalm talks about ה׳ as King and the nations trembling. It fits the story, since the ארון had just caused the פלשתים, a foreign nation, great trouble.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
"The Lord reigns; let the peoples tremble."
phrases.notes: תהלים 99:1

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר ה׳ מָלָךְ יִרְגְּזוּ עַמִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth answer to step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The song was תהלים 99, ה׳ מלך ירגזו עמים.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר נחמני: The Lord Reigns, Clothed in Majesty
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says the cows sang the psalm 'ה׳ מלך גאות לבש.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says: the song was 'The Lord reigns; He is clothed in majesty.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another אמורא gives his answer to the question of which song the cows sang. He picks a different psalm from רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי אלעזר and רבי שמואל בר נחמני choose a psalm that opens with 'ה׳ מלך‎,' ה׳ reigns. They differ only on which of these psalms it was.

keyTerms.meaning: He is clothed in, He wears

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani says:
"The Lord reigns; He is clothed in majesty."
phrases.notes: תהלים 93:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another answer to the question in step 30, next to רבי אלעזר's answer in step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cows sang תהלים 93, 'ה׳ מלך גאות לבש.'

steps.title: רבי יצחק נפחא: A Song to the Acacia ארון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק נפחא says the cows sang a song that is not a פסוק. The song speaks to the ארון and praises its wood, its gold, and the Torah inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק נפחא says: 'Sing, sing, acacia; rise up in all your glory; overlaid with golden embroidery, praised by the book of the palace, and beautiful with the finest jewels.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק נפחא gives the last answer. Unlike everyone before him, he does not quote a פסוק. He quotes a song addressed straight to the ארון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every earlier answer named a song found in תנ״ך. This answer is a poem that talks to the ארון itself, which was made of acacia wood and covered with gold. The 'דביר' in the song is the ספר תורה kept inside the ארון.

keyTerms.meaning: Acacia, the wood the ארון was made from
Here it means a book, the ספר תורה in the ארון

steps.confusionAlert: This song is not a פסוק from תנ״ך, so do not go looking for it in a חומש. It is a poem quoted only by the גמרא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha says:
"Sing, sing, acacia,
phrases.notes: He is talking to the ארון, which was built from acacia wood.

phrases.english: rise up in all your glory,
overlaid with golden embroidery,
praised by the book of the palace,
and beautiful with the finest jewels."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final answer to the question in step 30. It is the only one that is not a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The cows sang a poem praising the ארון: 'רוני רוני השיטה.'
steps.whatToRemember: The opinions on the cows' song are: אז ישיר, ואמרתם ביום ההוא, מזמור שירו לה׳ שיר חדש, ה׳ מלך ירגזו עמים, ה׳ מלך גאות לבש, and the poem 'רוני רוני השיטה.'

steps.title: רב אשי Moves the Song: What Did ישראל Say When the ארון Traveled?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי teaches רבי יצחק's song in a different setting. He attaches it to the פסוק of the ארון traveling in the desert and asks what ישראל said at that moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי teaches this statement of רבי יצחק on a different פסוק: 'And when the ארון traveled, משה said: Rise up, ה׳‎.' משה spoke, but what did ישראל say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of where רבי יצחק's statement belongs. This step sets up the question, and the next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק records only what משה said when the ארון moved. רב אשי's version asks what the people said, and that is where he places רבי יצחק's song. In this version the song was never about the cows.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi teaches it,
this statement of Rabbi Yitzchak,
on this verse: "And it was, when the Ark traveled,
Moshe said: Rise up, ה׳."
phrases.notes: במדבר 10:35

phrases.english: What did Israel say?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי מַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different setting for the statement of רבי יצחק in step 36.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What did ישראל say when the ארון traveled, since the פסוק records only משה's words?

steps.title: ישראל Sang 'Sing, Sing, Acacia'
steps.stepSummary: In רב אשי's version, רבי יצחק says ישראל sang the same poem to the ארון when it traveled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: they sang 'Sing, sing, acacia' and the rest of the song.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 37. The people sang רבי יצחק's poem to the ארון as it set out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the song are exactly the same. Only the occasion changes: in this version ישראל sang it in the desert, not the cows on the road to בית שמש.

keyTerms.meaning: And so on, the rest of the passage

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
"Sing, sing, acacia," etc.
phrases.notes: וכו׳ means the rest of the song, which was quoted in full in step 36.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק רוֹנִּי רוֹנִּי הַשִּׁיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ישראל sang 'רוני רוני השיטה' when the ארון traveled.

steps.title: Why the Persians Call a Book 'דביר'
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the Persian word 'דביר' for a book comes from a פסוק where the town דביר used to be called קרית ספר, 'town of the book.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: Where do the Persians get the custom of calling a book 'דביר'? From here: 'And the name of דביר before was קרית ספר.'
steps.whatsHappening: Because the song used the word דביר, the גמרא steps aside to explain it. רב shows that the word links to 'book' through a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the town דביר was once called קרית ספר. That pairs the name דביר with ספר, a book. So calling a book 'דביר' fits, which supports reading 'דביר ארמון' in the song as the ספר תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'like whom'; here, on what basis
Town of the book, the earlier name of דביר

phrases.english: Rav said:
On what basis do the Persians call
a book "devir"?
From here: "And the name of Devir before
was Kiryat Sefer."
phrases.notes: שופטים 1:11. 'קרית ספר' means 'town of the book.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כְּמַאן קָרוּ פָּרְסָאֵי לְסָפְרָא דְּבִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side note set off by the word דביר in the song of step 36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Persian word 'דביר' for a book comes from the פסוק that pairs דביר with קרית ספר.

steps.title: Why the Persians Call a נדה 'דשתנא'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds a second Persian word. They call a נדה 'דשתנא,' which comes from רחל's words 'דרך נשים לי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: On what basis do the Persians call a נדה 'דשתנא'? From here: 'For the way of women is upon me.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא is already discussing Persian words, it adds one more example in the same style. This finishes the side discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, רחל says 'דרך נשים לי' to mean she is a נדה. The Persian word 'דשתנא' sounds like a squeezed-together form of 'דרך נשים.'

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her monthly period
The Persian word for a נדה
The way of women, meaning the monthly period

steps.whatToRemember: Two Persian words are traced back to פסוקים: 'דביר' (book) comes from קרית ספר, and 'דשתנא' (נדה) comes from 'דרך נשים.'

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
On what basis do the Persians call a niddah "dashtana"?
From here: "For the way of women is upon me."
phrases.notes: בראשית 31:35. Say 'דרך נשים' quickly and you can hear 'דשתנא.'
